dmodule.title: Fault isolation: the console does not open

faultDescr.para: The console address does not open in the browser, or the console says it cannot reach the server.

isolationStep.action: Check that your device is on the same network as the server, or connected through the team's private network.
isolationStep.isolationStepQuestion: Is your device on the right network?

isolationStep.action: Check whether a VPN is running on your device.
Try to connect to the server over SSH, for example ssh yourusername@groundpi.local.
On the server, check the console service: systemctl status downlink-desk-web.
isolationStep.isolationStepQuestion: Does it show the service as active (running)?

isolationProcedureEnd.action: Connect your device to the server's network, or to the team's private network, and open the console address again.
The VPN is probably blocking local traffic. Turn on its option to allow local network access, or disconnect it, and open the console address again.

The server is off, has lost power or is not on the network. Check its power supply and network connection. A Raspberry Pi needs a proper 5 V, 2.5 A supply; a weak one causes random crashes. After power returns, the console starts by itself within a few minutes.

Restart the console service: sudo systemctl restart downlink-desk-web. If it does not stay running, read its log with journalctl -u downlink-desk-web -n 50 and report the error to whoever maintains the server.

The service is running, so the problem is between your device and the server. Check the address and port (8080 by default), and try the server's IP address in place of its name. If an update ran recently, check the About tab once you are in.
